rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not argue on behalf of wrongdoers against the innocent; here, do not defend the hypocrites for Ta'ma.
rows.anchor: ولا تكن لأجل الخائنين مخاصما لمن كان بريئا عن الذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ta'ma's people asked the Prophet to defend him and blame the Jew; the Prophet paused for revelation, which exposed Ta'ma as the liar and the Jew as innocent.
rows.anchor: لما التمسوا من الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام أن يذب عن طعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition does not prove the Prophet committed the forbidden act, so the verse does not establish a lapse in prophetic impeccability.
rows.anchor: النهي عن الشيء ة يقتضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer to the appeal to “seek forgiveness” is that the Prophet may naturally have leaned toward Ta'ma because he appeared to be Muslim; the command addressed that inclination.
rows.anchor: لعله مال طبعه إلى نصرة طعمة بسبب أنه كان في الظاهر من المسلمين فأمر بالستغفار لهذا القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the Prophet intended to rule from apparently credible testimony, then learned the witnesses had lied; he sought forgiveness for intending a ruling that would have been wrong, though he was excused.
rows.anchor: ثم لما أطلعه الله تعالى على كذب أولئك الشهود عرف أن ذلك القضاء لو وقع لكان خطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading takes the command to seek forgiveness as a request to seek forgiveness for those who were defending Ta'ma and trying to clear him.
rows.anchor: استغفر الله لأولئك الذين يذبون عن طعمة ويريدون أن يظهروا براءته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's favor means prophethood and His mercy means protection from error; without these, Ta'ma's faction would have led the Prophet into a false judgment.
rows.anchor: أن الله خصك بالفضل وهو النبوة ، وبالرحمة وهي العصمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ta'ma's people knew he was the thief but asked the Prophet to argue for his innocence and attribute the theft to the Jew.
rows.anchor: قوم طعمة كانوا قد عرفوا أن سارق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “lead you astray” means to draw the Prophet into a false, mistaken ruling.
rows.anchor: ومعنى يضلوك أي يلقوك في الحكم الباطل الخطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their collusion in sin and aggression and their false testimony make them, rather than the Prophet, the ones acting in error.
rows.anchor: بسبب تعاونهم على الإثم والعدوان وشهادتهم بالزور والبهتان

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal reads this as a promise of future protection: God will continue to guard the Prophet from their attempts to involve him in falsehood.
rows.anchor: قال القفال رحمه الله : وما يضرونك في المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the other reading, their efforts cause no harm because the Prophet did not fall into error: he based his judgment on the apparent evidence, as commanded.
rows.anchor: فأنت ما وقعت في الباطل ، لأنك بنيت الأمر على ظاهر الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If “no harm” promises future protection, the revelation of scripture and the charge to convey law confirm that divine wisdom will protect the messenger from doubt and misguidance.
rows.anchor: فكيف يليق بحكمته أن لا يعصمك عن الوقوع في الشبهات والضلالات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Prophet was excused for judging by appearances, the revealed law itself requires judgments from outward evidence, so doing so cannot harm him.
rows.anchor: وأوجب فيها بناء أحكام الشرع على الظاهر فكيف يضرك بناء الأمر على الظاهر

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal's first reading concerns religious knowledge: God disclosed the scripture's and wisdom's secrets and realities despite the Prophet's earlier lack of that knowledge, and will likewise protect him from future deception.
rows.anchor: قال القفال رحمه الله : هذه الآية تحتمل وجهين

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal's second reading is that God taught the Prophet the histories of earlier peoples and will teach him the hypocrites' schemes so he can guard against them.
rows.anchor: الوجه الثاني : أن يكون المراد : وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم من أخبار الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows the great honor of knowledge: human knowledge is only a little, yet God calls this little knowledge great, while calling the world's entire provision little.
rows.anchor: وهذا من أعظم الدلائل على أن العلم أشرف الفضائل والمناقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story follows the reminder that God protected believers from enemies (5:11) and consoles Muhammad: people have always envied those given great blessings, as the successive stories show.
rows.anchor: فذكر تعالى أن الأعداء يريدون إيقاع البلاء والمحنة بهم لكنه تعالى يحفظهم بفضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed link is to the passage cited as 5:15: this story and the law of retaliation it illustrates are among the Torah's concealed matters.
rows.anchor: وهذه القصة وكيفية إيجاب القصاص عليها من أسرار التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story may continue the account of Moses and the giants; it teaches the Jews that their ancestors' regret after sin resembled the regret in Adam's sons' story.
rows.anchor: القصة متعلقة بما قبلها ، وهي قصة محاربة الجبارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may connect to the claim “we are God's children and beloved”: descent from a revered prophet does not save unbelieving descendants, as Adam's son gained nothing from his father's standing.
rows.anchor: أي لا ينفعهم كونهم من أولاد الأنبياء مع كفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the People of the Book envied Muhammad and rejected him, the story warns them that envy brought its perpetrator to a disastrous end.
rows.anchor: لما كفر أهل الكتاب بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم حسدا أخبرهم الله تعالى بخبر ابن آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command “recite to them” is read either as addressing people generally or specifically the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: فيه قولان : أحدهما : واتل على الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first view identifies the two as Adam's biological sons, Abel and Cain.
rows.anchor: الأول : أنهما ابنا آدم من صلبه ، وهما هابيل وقابيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Abel was a shepherd and offered his best sheep, while Cain offered inferior grain; heavenly fire accepted Abel's offering, prompting Cain's envy and murderous intent.
rows.anchor: أن هابيل كان صاحب غنم ، وقابيل كان صاحب زرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says Adam had male-female twins and arranged cross-marriages; Cain refused to let his more beautiful twin sister marry Abel, and after their offerings were made the accepted offering led Cain to kill Abel out of envy.
rows.anchor: ما روي أن آدم عليه السلام كان يولد له في كل بطن غلام وجارية وكان يزوج البنت من بطن الغلام من بطن آخر

rows.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak say the two men were Israelites, not Adam's biological sons; the Israelite law of retaliation in 5:32 makes better sense if the crime occurred among Israelites.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : وهو قول الحسن والضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelite reading argues that the story's purpose is to expose the Jews' ancient, extreme envy: even seeing a God-accepted offering failed to make the envied man honor its recipient.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان المراد من ذكر هذه القصة بيان أن الحسد دأب قديم في بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers that these were Adam's own sons: Cain's ignorance of how to bury Abel until he saw the crow would be implausible if he were an Israelite.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن القول الأول هو الذي اختاره أكثر أصحاب الأخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading means the recitation is true and sound, coming from God.
rows.anchor: بالحق ، أي تلاوة متلبسة بالحق والصحة من عند الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading means the recitation is truthful and agrees with what is in the Torah and Gospel.
rows.anchor: أي تلاوة متلبسة بالصدق والحق موافقة لما في التوراة والإنجيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading takes “in truth” to mean with the proper purpose of condemning envy, which the idolaters and People of the Book showed toward Muhammad.
rows.anchor: بالحق ، أي بالغرض الصحيح وهو تقبيح الحسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story is recited for moral reflection, not idle entertainment; Razi links this lesson to the statement that earlier stories contain a lesson for people of understanding.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن المقصود بالذكر من الأقاصيص والقصص في القرآن العبرة

words: فتقبل من أحدهما ولم يتقبل من الآخر
rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes say acceptance was signaled when fire consumed the offering; Razi prefers this account because most commentators agree on it.
rows.anchor: قيل : كانت علامة القبول أن تأكله النار وهو قول أكثر المفسرين

words: فتقبل من أحدهما ولم يتقبل من الآخر
rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reverses the sign, saying that fire consuming the offering marked its rejection; Razi favors the majority view instead.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : علامة الرد أن تأكله النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further account says there were no poor people then to receive offerings, so fire descended from heaven and consumed them.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ما كان في ذلك الوقت فقير يدفع إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Piety is a condition for accepting deeds: as 22:37 says, what reaches God is not sacrificial meat or blood but the piety within people.
rows.anchor: إنما صار القربانين مقبولا والآخر مردودا لأن حصول التقوى شرط في قبول الأعمال

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet pointed to his heart when saying that piety is here, locating piety in the heart.
rows.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( التقوى هاهنا ) وأشار إلى القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True piety includes fearing one's own shortcomings in worship, seeking only God's pleasure in worship, and guarding against associating anything else with God; observing these conditions is difficult.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة التقوى أمور : أحدها : أن يكون على خوف

words: فتقبل من أحدهما ولم يتقبل من الآخر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account explains the different outcomes by saying one brother offered his best possession and the other his worst.
rows.anchor: وقيل في هذه القصة : إن أحدهما جعل قربانه أحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says Cain did not care whether his offering was accepted and would not give his sister in marriage to Abel.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنه أضمر أنه لا يبالي سواء قبل أو لم يقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation is that Cain was not pious or obedient, which is why God did not accept his offering.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان قابيل ليس من أهل التقوى والطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi supplies the omitted exchange: Cain asks why he should not kill Abel, explains that Abel's offering was accepted, and Abel replies that acceptance depends on piety, not on Abel's wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: لم تقتلني ؟ قال لأن قربانك صار مقبولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the statement about God accepting only the pious is a divine parenthetical address to Muhammad, explaining that Cain's offering was rejected because he lacked piety.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هذا من كلام الله تعالى لنبيه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi asks why Abel did not defend himself even if defense was obligatory or at least lawful; he answers that Abel addressed Cain before the attack to admonish him and deter intentional murder.
rows.anchor: هذا الكلام على سبيل الوعظ والنصيحة

words: ما أنا بباسط يدي إليك لأقتلك
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Cain waited until Abel slept, then killed him by striking his head with a large stone.
rows.anchor: ولهذا يروى أن قابيل صبر حتى نام هابيل فضرب رأسه بحجر كبير فقتله

words: ما أنا بباسط يدي إليك لأقتلك
rows.speaker: أهل العلم
rows.claim: Scholars say a defender must use the least force necessary and intend to repel the attack, not to kill; killing is permitted only if no lesser defense succeeds.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل العلم : الدافع عن نفسه يجب عليه أن يدفع

words: ما أنا بباسط يدي إليك لأقتلك
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say a person may choose to submit to being killed; Uthman did so, and the Prophet told Muhammad ibn Maslama to cover his face and be killed rather than kill.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : المقصود بالقتل إن أراد أن يستسلم جاز له ذلك

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet's instruction to Muhammad ibn Maslama was: cover your face, be God's slain servant, and do not be God's killing servant.
rows.anchor: ألق كمك على وجهك وكن عبد الله المقتول ولا تكن عبد الله القاتل

words: ما أنا بباسط يدي إليك لأقتلك
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The duty to defend oneself may differ across religious laws; Mujahid says self-defense was not permitted in that era.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : ءن الدفع عن النفس ما كان مباحا

words: لئن بسطت إلى يديك لتقتلني ما أنا بباسط
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional uses a verb but the response uses the active participle, stressing that Abel would not acquire the shameful identity of a killer; the prefixed bā reinforces the negation.
rows.anchor: والجواب : ليفيد أنه لا يفعل ما يكتسب به هذا الوصف الشنيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi frames the difficulty by comparing the claim that Cain will bear Abel's sin with the rule that no bearer carries another's burden.
rows.anchor: كيف يعقل أن يبوء القاتل بإثم المقتول

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, al-Hasan, and Qatada read “my sin” as the sin of killing me, with an omitted possessive, together with Cain's prior sins.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما وابن مسعود والحسن وقتادة رضي الله عنهم : معناه تحمل إثم قتلي

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the phrase as meaning that Cain will return to God.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : معناه ترجع إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the warning came before the murder: if Abel could only prevent a later attack by killing Cain first on suspicion, Abel would incur a grave sin, so he preferred Cain to bear it; conditional desire for another's sin here is obedience.
rows.anchor: قد ذكرنا أن هذا الكلام إنما دار بينهما عندما غلب على ظن المقتول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer is that Abel means he wants Cain to bear the punishment for murdering him; an oppressed person may wish that God punish the oppressor.
rows.anchor: أن المراد : إني أريد أن تبوء بعقوبة قتلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that on Judgment Day an oppressor who has no good deeds to repay the victim takes on the victim's sins as well as his own sin of murder.
rows.anchor: روي أن الظالم إذا لم يجد يوم القيامة ما يرضي خصمه

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators explain the phrase as meaning that Cain's soul made the murder easy for him; some instead say it emboldened him.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : سهلت له نفسه قتل أخيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi explains that awareness of murder's enormity initially makes it seem resistant and impossible; the soul's whisperings make it easy, as though turning a rebellious act into an obedient one.
rows.anchor: صار هذا الفعل سهلا عليه ، فكأن النفس جعلت بوساوسها العجيبة

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazila object that if God creates everything, the beautifying and easing of the murder should be attributed to God, not to Cain's soul.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : لو كان خالق الكل هو الله تعالى لكان ذلك التزيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi replies that acts are attributed to their motives; since God creates those motives, He is the creator of all acts.
rows.anchor: وجوابه : أنه لما أسندت الأفعال إلى الدواعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Cain did not know how to kill; Iblis demonstrated by striking a bird's head with a stone, and Cain later killed the sleeping Abel the same way.
rows.anchor: قيل : لم يدر قابيل كيف يقتل هابيل ، فظهر له إبليس

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said that every unjust killing leaves a share of its bloodguilt on Adam's first son because he was the first to institute murder.
rows.anchor: وعن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( لا تقتل نفس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Cain lost both worlds: in this life he angered his parents and remained condemned until the Resurrection, and in the next he faces great punishment.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : خسر دنياه وآخرته ، أما الدنيا فهو أنه أسخط والديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Cain fled to Aden in Yemen; Iblis falsely told him fire had accepted Abel's offering because Abel worshiped it, so Cain built a fire temple and became the first fire-worshiper.
rows.anchor: قيل : إن قابيل لما قتل أخاه هرب إلى عدن من أرض اليمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports place Abel's killing when he was twenty, either at the Aqabat Hira or, according to another account, in Basra where the Great Mosque stands.
rows.anchor: وروي أن هابيل قتل وهو ابن عشرين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Cain's formerly white body turned black; after he denied responsibility when Adam asked about Abel, Adam accused him, and Adam did not laugh for a hundred years afterward.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه لما قتله اسود جسد وكان أبيض

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf's author rejects the poem ascribed to Adam mourning Abel as a forged, faulty poem; Razi agrees, calling it too poor even for ignorant teachers and unworthy of Adam, whose knowledge God made a proof against the angels.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) يروى أنه رثاه بشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If believers turn from Islam and side with unbelievers, they should know God will bring other people who support His religion fully.
rows.anchor: يا أيها الذين آمنوا من يتول منكم الكفار فيرتد عن دينه فليعلم أن الله تعالى يأتي بأقوام آخرين

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says God knew some would apostatize after the Prophet's death, so He foretold a people He loves and who love Him; its fulfillment makes the verse a report of the unseen and a miracle.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن رحمه الله : علم الله أن قوما يرجعون عن الإسلام بعد موت نبيهم

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب والحسن وقتادة والضحاك وابن جريح
rows.claim: Ali, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Jurayj identify the promised people as Abu Bakr and his companions, who fought the apostates.
rows.anchor: فقال علي بن أبي طالب والحسن وقتادة والضحاك وابن جريح : هم أبو بكر وأصحابه

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says that after the Prophet died, the Arabs apostatized and hypocrisy became widespread; she describes the burden on Abu Bakr as something that would make firm mountains crumble.
rows.anchor: وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها : مات رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وارتدت العرب

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the promised people as the Ansar, who supported the Messenger and helped make the religion manifest.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي : نزلت الآية في الأنصار لأنهم هم الذين نصروا الرسول

rows.speaker: نجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the promised people as the people of Yemen.
rows.anchor: وقال نجاهد : نزلت في أهل اليمن

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report traced to the Prophet says that when this verse was revealed, he pointed to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and said the promised people were this man's people.
rows.anchor: وروي مرفوعا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما نزلت هذه الآية أشار إلى أبي موسى الأشعري

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Others identify them as Persians: a report says the Prophet struck Salman's shoulder and said he and his people were meant, adding that Persians would attain the religion even if it were at the Pleiades.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : هم الفرس لأنه روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما سئل عن هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the verse concerns Ali, arguing that at Khaybar the Prophet promised the standard to a man who loves God and His Messenger and is loved by them.
rows.anchor: أنه عليه السلام لما دفع الراية إلى علي عليه السلام يوم خيبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second argument for the Ali interpretation is that the following verse, 5:55, is about Ali, so the preceding verse should also concern him.
rows.anchor: قوله { إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين ءامنوا
